slides.title: The Du'a for a Heart That Keeps Slipping
slides.sub: Swipe for the du'a the Prophet ﷺ would say often, why he feared for hearts like ours, and 3 ways to stay steady.
slides.by: A letter from The Tazkiyyah Guide

blocks: You had a good Ramadan. Then it faded.
You left that talk on fire. A week later, nothing.
You promise yourself Fajr every night.
Some mornings, you miss it again.
You start to wonder if you were ever sincere.
If that's you, you're not a fake.
You're human, and your heart is doing what hearts do.
Hearts move. It's even in the word.
Qalb, the Arabic word for heart, comes from a root that means to turn over.
Even the best of creation ﷺ asked Allah to keep his heart steady.
He didn't ask once.
He said it often.
Anas said the Prophet ﷺ would often say:

quote.ar: يَا مُقَلِّبَ الْقُلُوبِ ثَبِّتْ قَلْبِي عَلَى دِينِكَ

blocks: "O Changer of the hearts, strengthen my heart upon Your religion."
Anas asked him: "Do you fear for us?"
He said: "Yes. Indeed the hearts are between two fingers of Allah's fingers, He changes them as He wills."
He feared for the companions.
So what about us?
Learn the words tonight. It takes two minutes.
Then say them like you mean it.

slides.after: You can't control how you'll feel tomorrow. You can control what you keep doing today.

blocks: ## 3 ways to stay steady
**1.** Make the du'a in sujud: *Ya Muqallib al-qulub, thabbit qalbi 'ala dinik.*
**2.** Keep one small deed you never drop. The most beloved deed to Allah is the most constant, even if it is small. *(Sahih al-Bukhari 6464)*
**3.** Add the du'a from the Qur'an: "Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us." *(Qur'an 3:8)*
A slipping heart isn't a lost heart.
It's a heart that needs this du'a.
Don't wait to feel steady before you make the du'a.
Make the du'a so that you become steady.
Start tonight, in your last sujud of 'Isha.
